items.statement: The maker identity and checker identity for any single exception's resolution are never the same person, with no override path.
items.enforcementPoint: ExceptionResolutionApi's approve/reject handler compares actor identity against the PROPOSED event's maker identity and rejects on equality before writing an event.

items.statement: An audit event, once written, is never updated or deleted through the application.
items.enforcementPoint: AuditEventStore exposes only an append operation; enforced by an automated test that attempts a mutation/delete call against the store's public API and asserts it does not exist / is rejected.

items.statement: An exception's resolvable state (derivable per REQ-5) has exactly one of: no resolution attempted, pending approval, approved, or rejected — never an ambiguous or contradictory combination.
items.enforcementPoint: The state-derivation function that replays events for an exception identity; covered by a unit test per possible event-sequence permutation up to 3 events.

items.statement: At most one PROPOSED event without a terminal APPROVED/REJECTED event may exist for a given exception identity at any time.
items.enforcementPoint: ExceptionResolutionApi's propose handler, which checks current derived state before accepting a new PROPOSED event and enforces this atomically via the store's conditional append (see REQ-6, REQ-7).

items.statement: No audit event or telemetry event ever contains a trade amount, counterparty identifier, settlement account number, or free-text evidence content in a telemetry payload.
items.enforcementPoint: Telemetry emission is restricted to a fixed, allow-listed field set (event type, exception identity, actor role, reason code, timestamp); enforced by a CI log-content scan test asserting telemetry payload keys are a subset of the allow-list.
